line.text: Think of a time the chatbot's reply to a customer went wrong and you wished it hadn't sent it. What did it say that made you wince?

Oh God, the bank one. A regular showed me a reply the chat had sent her that said "Dear valued customer, your feedback has been escalated to the relevant team." She was laughing, but I was mortified. Sure it sounded like her bank, not a café on a side street in Dublin 2. Someone was after giving a complaint to a robot and got a letter from a bank back, and I wanted to crawl under the counter.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: That sounds mortifying, especially with a regular reading it. What is it about that wording that made it sound like a bank to you, and what would you rather the chat had said in that spot?

It's the stiff, formal feel of it, like a letter with a reference number that nobody reads. Nobody at the counter talks like that, you know? I'd rather it said something like, sorry about that, I'm passing it straight to Gráinne, she'll be in touch. Short, warm, and like one of the lads had said it to her face.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: That gives me a clear picture of the feel you want. Should this apply to every reply the chat sends, or are there times it should sound more formal, like a refund or an allergy question?

Every reply, honestly. Allergies are the one place I'd want it careful and clear, not stiff. If it isn't sure, it says so plainly and tells them to ask at the counter, like I'd say it myself. Refunds, no such thing here, so the chat just says sorry and passes it to me.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: So every reply should sound short, warm and plain, like one of your staff talking to the customer, never like a formal letter. Allergy questions get careful, clear wording, and if it isn't sure it says so and tells them to ask at the counter. Refund complaints get an apology and get passed to you. Is that right?

Yeah, that's it exactly. Short, warm, like one of the lads at the counter, never a letter from the bank. Allergies, careful and clear, and if you're not sure, say so and send them to ask at the counter. No refunds or discounts, just a sorry and pass it on to me.

events.text: ShiftGuard thinks about what to ask next

line.text: Thanks, that's exactly the feel you want, and I've got it down. The chat's tone is set.

rule.title: Sound like a person at the counter
rule.ownerWords: Every reply should be short, warm and plain, like one of the lads at the counter talking to the customer, never a stiff letter from a bank. Allergy questions get careful, clear wording, and if the chat isn't sure, it says so plainly and tells them to ask at the counter. Refund complaints get a sorry and are passed to me.
rule.precise: Applies to every reply the chat sends. Replies must be short, warm and conversational, with no formal letter phrasing (for example 'Dear valued customer', 'escalated to the relevant team', or reference-number style wording). Allergy questions must be answered carefully and clearly; where the chat is not sure, it must say so plainly and direct the customer to ask at the counter. Refund or discount requests must not be promised or granted; the reply apologises and says it is being passed to the owner.
rule.exceptions: Allergy questions get more careful, clear wording rather than a looser tone. Refunds: none offered, the chat only apologises and passes it on.
rule.whyKind: Whether wording sounds stiff, warm or like a letter is a matter of feel, so it needs judgement rather than a fixed check.

violations.message: The reply opens with 'Dear valued customer' and uses 'escalated to the relevant team', which reads like a stiff formal letter rather than someone at the counter.
The reply is hyper-excited, with stacked exclamation marks and multiple emojis in a row, so it doesn't sound like a calm person at the counter.
The reply is a stiff, formal notice ('Thank you for your enquiry', 'Please be advised') rather than a short, warm, plain answer like someone at the counter would give.

events.howItWorks: The reply reads like one of the lads at the counter talking: short, warm, plain, calm, and careful in tone where allergies come up. The reply reads like a formal letter or bank notice, or is hyper-excited and cluttered with punctuation or emojis, so it no longer sounds like a person at the counter.
